references.text: Introduces that the Levites were not counted together with the other tribes, which verse 49 confirms as a direct command from the Lord.
Repeats that the Levites were not mustered among the children of Israel, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Explains the special role of the Levites—they were given to Aaron to serve in the tabernacle, which is why they were not counted with the other tribes.
The Lord commands Moses to count the Levites separately, confirming their distinct status from the other tribes.
The Levites are counted separately because they are to be a redemption for all the firstborn in Israel.
The Levites were set apart from the children of Israel and belong to the Lord, which explains why they were not mustered with the others.
In the second census, the Levites were again counted separately and not included among the children of Israel because they received no inheritance.
The tribe of Levi was set apart to carry the ark of the covenant and serve the Lord; therefore, they received no share of the land and were not counted with the others.
The Levites have no inheritance in Israel because the Lord is their inheritance, which justifies their distinct status.
